question: How does the immeasurable Lord appear as the measurable universe?
premises: The Lord is by nature free from measure.
He acts by the exercise of his own freedom.
By that freedom he makes himself into the moving and unmoving universe.
inference: Though immeasurable in essence, the Lord freely manifests himself as the measurable world of moving and unmoving beings.
plain_english: Even so, the god, who is himself beyond measure, by the exercise of his own freedom makes himself into the moving and unmoving universe.
